newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: BolsWessanen up on CSM bid talk.
newsitem.headline: BolsWessanen up on CSM bid talk.

text.p: Shares in Dutch food and drinks group BolsWessanen NV were higher on the AEX on Friday amid fresh market talk of a possible takeover by fellow Dutch food group CSM.
BolsWessanen shares were up 1.10 guilders at 32.30, while CSM was trading down 1.40 guilders at 94.20 in a generally buoyant market.
A CSM spokeswoman categorically denied that the firm planned to make an offer for BolsWessanen.
"This is a surprise to us. The company absolutely denies it has any plans to approach BolsWessanen," she said.
BolsWessanen said it would not comment on market rumours.

Amsterdam dealers said there was considerable talk in the market about a possible takeover by CSM, with one quoting share-swap terms of one CSM share plus 15 guilders for every three BolsWessanen shares.
But Dutch food sector analysts said they considered a bid very unlikely.
"CSM is not interested in having a position in the cheese, beverages or cereals markets, which is most of BolsWessanen," said one analyst who asked not to be identified.
"With (BolsWessanen) shares lagging the market, there's not much downside risk in playing the shares speculatively," he said.

BolsWessanen shares jumped last week on speculation the company was being stalked by British drinks group Grand Metropolitan. The shares fell back after the company issued an official denial. -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040
